Name: ND Network Description MODELs
Notes: The Network Description Model describes the basic physical network and is divided into a number of separate submodels covering different aspects of the Network. For ease of understanding, the submodels are presented one at a time, each describing only a small set of related concepts.
Exclusion

For FTS, a link can occur between
  * 2 points.
  * 2 zones (through centroid Points).
  * a point and a zone.
This is true for ROUTE LINK, TIMING LINK and SERVICE LINK.

Name: FLEXIBLE POINT PROPERTIES
Notes: Set of characteristics describing the possible flexibility of POINTs.

Name: FLEXIBLE LINK PROPERTIES
Notes: Set of properties describing the flexible characteristics of a LINK.

Name: FLEXIBLE LINE
Notes:
Specialisation of LINE for flexible service.
NOTE1: As the service on a LINE may not all be flexible, flexibility itself is described at JOURNEY PATTERN level (meaning that a separate JOURNEY PATTERN is needed for each type of flexibility available for the line).
NOTE2: Types of flexible services include: Virtual line services; Flexible service with a main route; Corridor services; Fixed stop area-wide flexible services; Free area-wide flexible services; Mixed combinations of flexible services of different types; Mixed combinations of flexible and regular services.

Name: FLEXIBLE ROUTE
Notes:
Specialisation of ROUTE for flexible service.
NOTE: May include both point and zonal areas and ordered and unordered sections.

Name: ACTIVATED EQUIPMENT
Notes: An equipment activated by the passage of a vehicle at an ACTIVATION POINT or on an ACTIVATION LINK.

Name: ACTIVATION POINT
Notes:
A POINT where a control process is activated when a vehicle passes it.
NOTE: EQUIPMENT may be needed for the activation.

Name: TYPE OF ACTIVATION
Notes: A classification of real-time processes that are activated when vehicles pass an ACTIVATION POINT or an ACTIVATION LINK.

Name: TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT
Notes: A POINT where the traffic flow can be influenced, e.g., traffic lights (lanterns), barriers.

Name: ACTIVATION LINK
Notes: A LINK where a control process is activated when a vehicle passes it.

Name: TYPE OF TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT
Notes: A classification of TRAFFIC CONTROL POINTs.

Name: ACTIVATION ASSIGNMENT
Notes:
An assignment of an ACTIVATION POINT or LINK to an ACTIVATED EQUIPMENT, related in its turn to a TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT.
NOTE: The considered ACTIVATION POINT or LINK will be used to influence the control process for that TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT (e.g., to fix priorities as regards the processing of competing requests from different ACTIVATION POINTs/LINKs).
Exclusion

Name: BEACON POINT
Notes: A POINT where a beacon or similar device to support the automatic detection of vehicles passing by is located.

Name: RELIEF POINT
Notes:
A TIMING POINT where a relief is possible, i.e., a driver may take on or hand over a vehicle.
NOTE: The vehicle may sometimes be left unattended even though it has passengers on board.

Name: GARAGE
Notes:
A facility used for parking and maintaining vehicles.
NOTE1: PARKING POINTs in a GARAGE are called GARAGE POINTs.
NOTE2: Such a facility is often called a depot.

Name: CREW BASE
Notes: A place where operating employees (e.g., drivers) report on and register their work.

Name: PARKING POINT
Notes:
A TIMING POINT where vehicles may stay unattended for a long time.
NOTE1: A vehicle's return to park at a PARKING POINT marks the end of a BLOCK.
NOTE2: Normally there are no passengers on board at a PARKING POINT.

Name: GARAGE POINT
Notes: A subtype of PARKING POINT located in a GARAGE.

Classifying instruction to direct user e.g.,
up / down / level, 
left / right,
backward /forward

Name: ROUTE INSTRUCTION
Notes:
A view providing Information for a human readable instruction as to how to follow a step on the ROUTE.
NOTE: Data may be derived from underlying route link and spatial PROJECTION of ROUTE LINK and ROUTE POINTs.

Name: ALLOWED LINE DIRECTION
Notes:
An allowed DIRECTION that can be used on a given ROUTE.
NOTE: This can be used to validate the selection of allowed values.

Name: LINE
Notes: A group of ROUTEs which is generally known to the public by a similar name or number.

Name: GROUP OF LINES
Notes: A grouping of lines which will be commonly referenced for a specific purpose.

Name: DESTINATION DISPLAY VARIANT
Notes: An advertised destination of a specific JOURNEY PATTERN, usually displayed on a headsign or at other on-board locations.

Name: NETWORK
Notes: A named grouping of LINEs under which a transport network is known.

Name: TYPE OF LINE
Notes: A classification for LINEs.

Name: DESTINATION DISPLAY
Notes: An advertised destination of a specific JOURNEY PATTERN, usually displayed on a headsign or at other on-board locations.

Name: VIA
Notes: A secondary heading relevant for a certain part of the JOURNEY PATTERN advertising an onward intermediate destination to supplement the advertised (final) destination of DESTINATION DISPLAY.

Name: TYPE OF VIA
Notes: A classification for VIAs, e.g. as a specific stop point, as a place name, as a general phrase.

Name: WIRE JUNCTION
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE POINT used to describe a wire network.

Name: WIRE ELEMENT
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE LINK used to describe a wire network.

Name: INFRASTRUCTURE POINT
Notes: A specialisation of POINT representing a junction point in the physical network (e.g., RAILWAY JUNCTION, ROAD JUNCTION, etc.).

Name: INFRASTRUCTURE LINK
Notes: A specialisation of LINK representing a link between two points in the physical network (e.g., RAILWAY ELEMENT, ROAD ELEMENT, etc.).

Name: ROAD JUNCTION
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE POINT used to describe a road network.

Name: RAILWAY ELEMENT
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE LINK used to describe a railway network.

Name: ROAD ELEMENT
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE LINK used to describe a road network.

Name: RAILWAY JUNCTION
Notes: A type of INFRASTRUCTURE POINT used to describe a railway network.

Name: IMPOSSIBLE MANOEUVRE
Notes: A specification of an impossible move for a certain type of vehicle; it specifies from which INFRASTRUCTURE LINK to which other (adjacent) INFRASTRUCTURE LINK a certain VEHICLE TYPE cannot proceed, due to physical restrictions.
exclusion

Name: VEHICLE TYPE AT POINT
Notes:
The number of vehicles of a specified VEHICLE TYPE which may wait at a specified POINT at any one time.
NOTE: If the capacity is 0, then that type of vehicle may not stop there.

Name: MEETING RESTRICTION
Notes: A pair of INFRASTRUCTURE LINKs where vehicles of specified VEHICLE TYPEs are not allowed to meet.

Name: OVERTAKING POSSIBILITY
Notes: NETWORK RESTRICTION specifying a POINT or a LINK where vehicles of specified VEHICLE TYPEs are or are not allowed to overtake each other.

Name: ROUTE POINT
Notes: A POINT used to define the shape of a ROUTE through the network.

Name: ROUTE
Notes:
An ordered list of located POINTs defining one single path through the road (or rail) network.
NOTE: A ROUTE may pass through the same POINT more than once.

Name: ROUTE LINK
Notes: An oriented link between two ROUTE POINTs allowing the definition of a unique path through the network.

Name: POINT ON ROUTE
Notes: A ROUTE POINT used to define a ROUTE with its order on that ROUTE.

Name: TURN STATION
Notes: A place (often a terminus) where a vehicle can reverse its direction (from a ROUTE to another of opposite DIRECTION).

Name: DIRECTION
Notes: A classification for the general orientation of ROUTEs.

Name: MODE RESTRICTION ASSESSMENT
Notes: Qualification of a ROUTE LINK resulting from the analysis of restrictions concerning the related INFRASTRUCTURE LINKs.

Name: POINT ON LINE SECTION
Notes: Association of a POINT with a COMMON SECTION.

Name: TYPE OF LINE SECTION POINT
Notes: A classification of a POINT ON LINE SECTION to indicate how it should be presented, for example as a main station, optional stop, etc.
A LINE NETWORK allows the network topology to be assembled as a list of linked sections, which altogether make up a graph. It can be used for example to underpin an interactive map.

Name: LINE NETWORK
Notes:
The topological structure of a NETWORK as a graph of LINE SECTIONs.
NOTE: This allows the branches and loops of a LINE or LINEs to be described as a whole.

Name: LINE SECTION
Notes: A section of a LINE NETWORK comprising one or more POINTS or LINKS connecting two end points.
Exclusion
A LINE NETWORK allows the network topology to be assembled as a list of linked sections, which altogether make up aa graph. It can be used for example to underpin an interactive map.

A LINE NETWORK allows the network topology to be described as a mesh of LINE SECTIONS.
A LINK SEQUENCE, can be considered as a sequence of POINTs ON SECTION. A LINE SECTION is a specialisation of LINK SEQUENCE and can similarly be considered as a as a sequence of POINTs ON LINE SECTION.

Additionally a LINE SECTION can specify a set of points in the reverse direction (to cover the case where the points differ in different directions). 
If two LINE SECTIONs reference the same point, they are deemed to be connected at that point.

A POINT ON LINE SECTION may be annotated to indicate it should be presented with particular features, for example as a main station, accessible, etc.
A LINE NETWORK allows the network topology to be assembled as a list of linked sections, which altogether make up aa graph. It can be used for example to underpin an interactive map.

PATH LINK
Notes:
A path within a SITE connecting between any two SITE COMPONENTs (e.g., a STOP PLACE ENTRANCE, ACCESS SPACE, QUAY, BOARDING POSITIONs, etc.), or PATH JUNCTIONs.
NOTE: Each link represents a step in a possible route for pedestrians, cyclists or other out-of-vehicle passengers within or between two places.

Name: SITE PATH LINK END
Notes: Beginning or end for a SITE PATH LINK, associated with a given SITE ELEMENT, PATH JUNCTION or DECK COMPONENT; may also be linked to a specific LEVEL of a SITE.

Name: PATH JUNCTION
Notes: A designated point, inside or outside of a STOP PLACE or POINT OF INTEREST, at which two or more PATH LINKs may connect or branch.
Also alias as SITE PATH JUNCTION.
Also alias as SITE PATH LINK
Also alias as SITE NAVIGATION PATH.
NAVIGATION PATH, PATH LINK and PATH LINK JUNCTION can also be used to connect PLACES and POINTs that are not part of a SITE. In this case

Name: SITE COMPONENT
Notes:
An element of a SITE describing a part of its structure.
NOTE: SITE COMPONENTs share common properties for data management, accessibility and other features.

Name: ENTRANCE
Notes: A physical entrance or exit to/from a SITE; may be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of access.

Name: ACCESS ZONE
Notes: A ZONE for which the duration needed to reach a particular STOP POINT is considered to be the same.

Name: VEHICLE ENTRANCE
Notes:
A physical entrance or exit to/from a SITE for a VEHICLE.
NOTE: May be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of vehicle access.

Name: SITE
Notes: A well known PLACE to which passengers may refer to indicate the origin or a destination of a trip.

Name: LEVEL
Notes:
An identified storey (ground, first, basement, mezzanine, etc.) within an interchange building or SITE on which SITE COMPONENTs reside.
NOTE: A PATH LINK may connect components on different levels.

Name: SERVICE SITE
Notes: A sub-type of SITE which is of specific interest for the operator (e.g., where a joint service or a joint fee is proposed), other than a STOP PLACE.

Name: SITE ELEMENT
Notes: A specialisation of ADDRESSABLE PLACE describing common properties of a SITE or a SITE COMPONENT, including accessibility.

Name: SITE STRUCTURE
Notes: A building or a separate part thereof within a SITE.

Name: LEVEL IN STRUCTURE
Notes: <font color="#445469">A LEVEL, i.e., storey in a building, that is accessible in a SITE STRUCTURE with its relative lateral order in that SITE STRUCTURE counted from the bottom and upwards.</font>

Name: GROUP OF SITES
Notes: A grouping of SITEs for a particular functional purpose, usually the SITEs will be non-contiguous, such as the airports for a CITY.

Name: TYPE OF ENTRANCE
Notes: A classification for ENTRANCE for example as an opening, door, barrier etc.

Name: STOP PLACE
Notes:
A place comprising one or more locations where vehicles may stop and where passengers may board or leave vehicles or prepare their trip.
NOTE: A STOP PLACE will usually have one or more well-known names.

Name: QUAY
Notes:
A place such as platform, stance, or quay side where passengers have access to PT vehicles, Taxis, cars or other means of transportation.
NOTE1: A QUAY may serve one or more VEHICLE STOPPING PLACEs and be associated with one or more SCHEDULED STOP POINTS.
NOTE2: A QUAY may contain other sub QUAYs.
NOTE3: A child QUAY must be physically contained within its parent QUAY.

Name: TYPE OF STOP PLACE
Notes: A classification for STOP PLACEs (e.g., complex, simple, multimodal, etc.).

Name: STOP PLACE SPACE
Notes: A physical area within a STOP PLACE, for example, a QUAY, BOARDING POSITION, ACCESS SPACE or EQUIPMENT PLACE.

Name: STOP PLACE ENTRANCE
Notes: A physical entrance or exit to/from a STOP PLACE for a Passenger; may be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of access.

Name: BOARDING POSITION
Notes: A location within a QUAY from which passengers may directly board, or onto which passengers may directly alight from a VEHICLE.

Name: STOP PLACE VEHICLE ENTRANCE`
Notes: A physical entrance or exit to/from a STOP PLACE for a vehicle.

Name: STOP PLACE COMPONENT
Notes:
An element of a STOP PLACE describing part of its structure.
NOTE: STOP PLACE COMPONENTs share common properties for data management, accessibility and other features.

Name: TYPE OF QUAY
Notes: A classification for QUAYs.

Name: TYPE OF BOARDING POSITION
Notes: A classification for BOARDING POSITIONs.

Name: ACCESS SPACE
Notes:
A passenger area within a STOP PLACE such as a concourse or booking hall, immigration hall or security area that is accessible by passengers, but without a direct access to vehicles.
NOTE: Direct access to a VEHICLE is always from a QUAY and/or BOARDING POSITION.

Name: TYPE OF PASSAGE
Notes: A classification for spaces to express how the space can be used as a passage (e.g., as pathway, corridor, overpass, underpass, tunnel, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF ACCESS SPACE
Notes: A classification for ACCESS SPACE, e.g. forecourt ticket hall, shop, etc.

Name: FLEXIBLE QUAY
Notes: A physical ZONE such as a section of a road where a flexible service is available on demand.

Name: HAIL AND RIDE AREA
Notes: Specialisation of a FLEXIBLE QUAY defining a physical section of road between a start and end point within which a Hail and Ride service is available.

Name: FLEXIBLE STOP ASSIGNMENT
Notes:
The allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (i.e., a STOP POINT of a SERVICE PATTERN or JOURNEY PATTERN) to a specific FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE, and also possibly a FLEXIBLE AREA or HAIL AND RIDE AREA.
NOTE: May be subject to a VALIDITY CONDITION.

Name: FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE
Notes:
A specialisation of the STOP PLACE describing a stop of a FLEXIBLE SERVICE.
NOTE1: It may be composed of FLEXIBLE AREAs or HAIL AND RIDE AREAs identifying the catchment areas for flexible services (when they use areas or flexible quays).
NOTE2: Some FLEXIBLE SERVICEs also use regular STOP PLACEs for their stops.

Name: FLEXIBLE AREA
Notes: Specialisation of a FLEXIBLE QUAY (which is abstract) to identify what is the catchment area for a flexible service (so that a stop finder can find the nearest available types of transport).

Name: POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY
Notes:
A logical hierarchy for organizing POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATIONs.
NOTE: A POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION can belong to more than one hierarchy.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST ENTRANCE
Notes: Specialisation of ENTRANCE to enter/exit a POINT OF INTEREST.

Name: TYPE OF POINT OF INTEREST SPACE
Notes: A classification for POINT OF INTEREST SPACEs.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST COMPONENT
Notes: Specialisation of SITE COMPONENT for COMPONENT of POINT OF INTEREST.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION
Notes: A classification of a POINT OF INTEREST that may be used in a POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY to categorise the point by nature of interest using a systematic taxonomy, for example Museum, Football, Stadium, etc.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST VEHICLE ENTRANCE
Notes: A physical entrance for VEHICLEs to enter or exit a POINT OF INTEREST.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST SPACE
Notes: A specialisation of POINT OF INTEREST COMPONENT representing a physical area within the POINT OF INTEREST, such as a concourse.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST
Notes: A type of PLACE to or through which passengers may wish to navigate as part of their journey and which is modelled in detail by journey planners.

Name: POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBER
Notes: The POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION and POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBER are used to encode a hierarchy of classifications to index and find different types of POINT OF INTEREST; for example, Educational Building -> School -> Primary School, or Cultural Attraction -> Museum -> Art Museum. NOTE: POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBERSHIP does not have to be disjoint, i.e., the same category may appear in more than one classification.
PASSENGER EQUIPMENT is either fixed or on-board

Name: EQUIPMENT PLACE
Notes: A SITE COMPONENT containing EQUIPMENT.
PLACE EQUIPMENT is fixed

Name: EQUIPMENT POSITION
Notes: The precise position within an EQUIPMENT PLACE where particular equipment is placed.
PASSENGER EQUIPMENT is either fixed or on-board
PLACE EQUIPMENT is fixed

Name: TROLLEY STAND EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of STOP PLACE EQUIPMENT describing trolley stands.

Name: SITE EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PLACE EQUIPMENT describing common properties of EQUIPMENT for SITEs (e.g., for LUGGAGE LOCKER, WAITING EQUIPMENT, TROLLEY STAND, etc.),

Name: SEATING EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of WAITING EQUIPMENT describing the properties of seating

Name: WAITING ROOM EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of WAITING EQUIPMENT describing waiting rooms (number of seats, type, FACILITIEs, etc.).

Name: WAITING EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of SITE EQUIPMENT describing common features of waiting areas (shelter, waiting room, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF WAITING ROOM
Notes: A classification for WAITING ROOM EQUIPMENT.

Name: TYPE OF SHELTER
Notes: A classification for SHELTER EQUIPMENT.

Name: LUGGAGE LOCKER EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of SITE EQUIPMENT describing luggage lockers.

Name: SHELTER EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of WAITING EQUIPMENT describing a shelter.

Name: TYPE OF SEATING EQUIPMENT
Notes: A classification for SEATING EQUIPMENT.

Name: TYPE OF LUGGAGE LOCKER
Notes: A classification for LUGGAGE LOCKER EQUIPMENT (e.g., left luggage, lockers, bike carriage, porterage, free trolleys, paid trolleys).

Name: HELP POINT EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT describing a HELP POINT.

Name: PASSENGER BEACON EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT describing a beacon to assist disabled passengers.

Name: TYPE OF PASSENGER BEACON
Notes: A classification for a PASSENGER BEACON.

Name: PASSENGER BEACON PROTOCOL
Notes: A classification of the device communication protocol used for a PASSENGER BEACON EQUIPMENT (iBEAcon, VDV431, EDDYSTONE, etc.).

Name: RUBBISH DISPOSAL
Notes: Specialisation of EQUIPMENT describing rubbish disposal features, (permitted rubbish types, etc.)

Name: PASSENGER SAFETY EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT describing passenger safety features of a SITE.

Name: SANITARY EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT describing sanitary facilities (WC, shower, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF SANITARY FACILITY
Notes: A classification for SANITARY EQUIPMENT (e.g., toilet, wheelchair access toilet, shower, baby change, wheelchair baby change)

Name: TICKET VALIDATOR EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT (PLACE EQUIPMENT) describing ticket validators.

Name: TICKETING EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialization of PASSENGER EQUIPMENT for ticketing.

Name: METHOD OF QUEUE MANAGEMENT
Notes: A classification of method used to manage a queue, e.g., rails, parallel rails, ticket, appointment, etc.

Name: TYPE OF LIGHTING
Notes: A classification of a PLACE LIGHTING as well-lit, poorly lit, etc.

Name: LIGHTING ON METHOD
Notes: A classification of methods for turning lights on and off.

Name: TYPE OF CROSSING
Notes: A classification for road CROSSING EQUIPMENT.

Name: ENTRANCE ATTENTION METHOD
Notes: A classification of method used to invoke opening of ENTRANCE EQUIPMENT.

Name: ENTRANCE EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing an equipment for an ENTRANCE (door, barrier, revolving door, etc.).

Name: CROSSING EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing a road crossing for pedestrians (zebra, pedestrian lights, acoustic device sensors, tactile guide strips, etc.).

Name: ROUGH SURFACE
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT for rough surfaces, giving properties of surface texture, mainly for impaired person information.

Name: ACCESS EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PLACE EQUIPMENT describing common properties of equipment with which to access a SITE (e.g., lifts, entrances, stairs, ramps, etc.).

Name: QUEUING EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing queuing equipment or features.

Name: PLACE LIGHTING
Notes: Specialisation of PLACE EQUIPMENT describing the lighting (e.g., always on, etc.).

Name: RAMP EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing a ramp (provides ramp characteristics like length, gradient, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF SURFACE
Notes: A classification for ROUGH SURFACE types.

Name: LIFT EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing a lift (depth, maximum load, etc.).

Name: TRAVELATOR EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing a travelator (provides attributes such as speed, energy saving, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF HANDRAIL
Notes: A classification of a handrail (one side, both sides, continuous, etc.).

Name: ESCALATOR EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of STAIR EQUIPMENT describing an ESCALATOR.

Name: STAIRCASE EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of STAIR EQUIPMENT describing a staircase.

Name: STAIR EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing a stepped feature (stair, escalator, staircase, etc.)

Name: LIFT CALL EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PLACE ACCESS EQUIPMENT describing means of calling a lift (button height, buttons, etc.).

Name: SIGN EQUIPMENT
Notes: Specialisation of PLACE EQUIPMENT describing common properties of a sign (heading signs, etc.).

Name: GENERAL SIGN
Notes: Specialisation of SIGN EQUIPMENT describing a sign which is neither a HEADING SIGN nor a PLACE SIGN.

Name: HEADING SIGN
Notes: Specialisation of SIGN EQUIPMENT describing a sign showing a heading; provides information such as DIRECTION name, LINE name, line number etc.

Name: PLACE SIGN
Notes: Specialisation of SIGN EQUIPMENT describing a sign that shows the name of a STOP PLACE.

Name: AVAILABILITY OF ASSISTANCE
Notes: Summary indication of when assistance is available, e.g., always, never, staff hours only, peak times, etc.

Name: LOCAL SERVICE
Notes:
A named service relating to the use of the SITE or transport services at a particular location, for example porterage, assistance for disabled users, booking offices, etc.
NOTE1: The service may have a VALIDITY CONDITION associated with it.
NOTE2: A LOCAL SERVICE is treated as a form of non-material EQUIPMENT.

Name: ASSISTANCE SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing assistance services, providing information such as language, accessibility trained staff, etc.

Name: TYPE OF EMERGENCY SERVICE
Notes: A classification of emergency services (e.g., police, first aid, SOS point, CCTV, etc.).

Name: CUSTOMER SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing common properties of customer services, (e.g., lost property service, meeting point, complaints service, etc.).

Name: LOST PROPERTY SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of CUSTOMER SERVICE of describing lost property services

Name: TYPE OF LOCAL SERVICE
Notes: A generic (abstract) classification of LOCAL SERVICEs.

Name: LEFT LUGGAGE SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing left luggage amenities; provides information such as self-service locker, left luggage office,, etc.

Name: LUGGAGE SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing luggage carrying services (e.g., luggage trolley, free to use, etc.).

Name: TICKETING SERVICE
Notes: Specialization of LOCAL SERVICE describing ticketing services, such as a ticket counter, online purchase, etc.; also associated with payment method and TYPE OF TICKET.

Name: TYPE OF ACCESSIBILITY TOOLS
Notes: A classification of ACCESSIBILITY TOOLS used by or available from ASSISTANCE SERVICE (e.g., wheelchair, walking stick, audio navigator, visual navigator, etc.)

Name: MEETING POINT SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of CUSTOMER SERVICE describing a meeting point (provides characteristics such as description, label, etc.).

Name: COMPLAINTS SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of CUSTOMER SERVICE describing complaint services.

Name: TYPE OF ASSISTANCE SERVICE
Notes: A classification of an ASSISTANCE SERVICE (e.g., boarding assistance, onboard assistance, porterage, foreign language, sign language translation, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF STAFFING
Notes: A classification for the availability of the STAFF associated with an ASSISTANCE SERVICE (e.g., full time, part time)

Name: MONEY SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing available money services (e.g., bureau de change, ATM, etc.).

Name: TYPE OF CATERING SERVICE
Notes: A classification of CATERING SERVICE (e.g., beverage vending machine, buffet, food vending machine, restaurant, snacks, trolley service, no beverages available, no food available).

Name: TYPE OF RETAIL SERVICE
Notes: A classification of RETAIL SERVICE (e.g., food, newspaper tobacco, health hygiene beauty, fashion accessories, bank finance insurance, tourism, photo booth)

Name: TYPE OF COMMUNICATION SERVICE
Notes: A classification of COMMUNICATION SERVICE (e.g., free wifi, public wifi, phone, mobile coverage, internet, video entertainment, audio entertainment, post box, post office, business services).

Name: CATERING SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing available catering services.

Name: COMMUNICATION SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing available communication services.

Name: TYPE OF MONEY SERVICE
Notes: A classification of MONEY SERVICE (e.g., as cash machine, bank, insurance, bureau de change),

Name: TYPE OF HIRE SERVICE
Notes: A classification of HIRE SERVICEs (e.g., as car hire, motorcycle hire, cycle hire, recreational device hire).

Name: RETAIL SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing available retail services.

Name: HIRE SERVICE
Notes: Specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE describing the types of available hire services (e.g., cycle hire, car hire).

Name: CYCLE STORAGE EQUIPMENT
Notes: A specialisation of PLACE EQUIPMENT describing cycle parking equipment.

Name: TYPE OF CYCLE STORAGE EQUIPMENT
Notes: A classification of CYCLE STORAGE EQUIPMENT (e.g., racks, bars, railings, etc.)

Name: VEHICLE RELEASE EQUIPMENT
Notes: A specialisation of INSTALLED EQUIPMENT describing equipment for releasing a vehicle from a lock so it can be used.

Name: ASSISTANCE BOOKING SERVICE
Notes: A specialisation of LOCAL SERVICE providing information about how to book assistance for wheelchair and disabled users.

Name: TYPE OF PARKING USER
Notes: A classification of a type of parking user, e.g., disabled, season ticket holder, anonymous, etc.

Name: PARKING COMPONENT
Notes: Generic COMPONENT of a PARKING (e.g., PARKING AREA or PARKING BAY)

Name: PARKING
Notes: Designated locations for leaving vehicles such as cars, motorcycles and bicycles.

Name: PARKING ENTRANCE FOR VEHICLES
Notes: An entrance for vehicles to the PARKING from the road.

Name: PARKING PASSENGER ENTRANCE
Notes: A pedestrian, wheelchair or other out-of-vehicle-mode entrance to the PARKING.

Name: PARKING BAY
Notes: A place to park an individual vehicle.

Name: PARKING CAPACITY
Notes: PARKING properties providing information about its CAPACITY.

Name: PARKING PROPERTIES
Notes: PARKING specific properties other than its capacity.

Name: PARKING AREA
Notes: A marked zone within a PARKING containing PARKING BAYs.

Name: PARKING COMPONENT PROPERTIES
Notes: <font color="#0f0f0f">A set of public facing characteristics of a PARKING COMPONENT facilitating the recognition of the component by a traveller.</font>

Name: TYPE OF PARKING
Notes: A classification for a PARKING, e.g., on street, multi-storey, parking lot, etc.

Name: TYPE OF PARKING STAY
Notes: A classification of the type of parking stay, e.g., long term, short term; may be used to choose pricing criteria.

Name: PARKING ACCESS SPACE
Notes: An area for pedestrian access within a PARKING.

Name: TYPE OF PARKING PAYMENT PROCESS
Notes: A classification of a type of parking payment process, pay at display, pay by mobile, pay at exit,Â Â

Name: TYPE OF PARKING RESERVATION
Notes: A classification of a type of parking reservation process for the PARKING, e.g. no reservations, reservations required, reservations possible, etc.

Name: PARKING PRIORITY CATEGORY
Notes: Characterisation of the priority to park according to some policy rules, e.g. handicapped users during shopping hours, staff, etc

Name: VEHICLE QUAY ALIGNMENT
Notes: The alignment of a particular QUAY with a vehicle as the result of positioning a VEHICLE at a particular VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE.

Name: VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE
Notes:
A place on the vehicle track where vehicles stop in order for passengers to board or alight from a vehicle.
NOTE1: A vehicle track is located on the respective INFRASTRUCTURE LINK for the MODE (RAILWAY ELEMENT of rail network, ROAD ELEMENT of road network, etc.).
NOTE2: A VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE may be served by one or more QUAYs.

Name: VEHICLE POSITION ALIGNMENT
Notes: The alignment of a particular BOARDING POSITION with the entrance of a VEHICLE as the result of positioning the VEHICLE at a particular VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE.

Name: VEHICLE STOPPING POSITION
Notes:
The stopping position of a vehicle or one of its components as a Location.
NOTE1: May be specified as a ZONE corresponding to the bounding polygon of the vehicle, or one or more POINTs corresponding to parts of the vehicle such as a door.
NOTE2: If given as a single point, indicates the position for the door relative to an indicated side of the vehicle.

Name: TYPE OF RELATION TO VEHICLE
Notes: A classification of the way a VEHICLE STOPPING POSITION is used (e.g., front left, front right, back left, back right, driver left, driver right).
Relative position of stopping position to vehicle, e.g., vehicle front left, vehicle front right, vehicle back left, vehicle back right, driver left, driver right, etc.

Name: TAXI PARKING AREA
Notes: A specific area where any taxi is able to safely park for a long period.

Name: TAXI STAND
Notes: A set of spots where any taxi is able to safely stop for a short period of time to load passengers.

Name: TAXI RANK
Notes: A STOP PLACE specifically for taxis, comprising one or more TAXI STANDs.

The exact location of the EQUIPMENT within the bay can be given by an EQUIPMENT PLACE.

Name: RECHARGING BAY
Notes: A PARKING BAY specifically equipped for recharging VEHICLEs.

Name: RECHARGING STATION
Notes: A PARKING with bays specifically equipped for recharging VEHICLEs.

Name: NAVIGATION PATH
Notes: A designated path between two SITES or SITE COMPONENTs.

Also alias as SITE NAVIGATION PATH.

Name: TP Passenger Information Display Assignment MODEL
TYPE OF JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: A classification of JOURNEY PATTERNs used to distinguish categories of JOURNEY PATTERN other than SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN and DEAD RUN PATTERN.

Name: POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: A SCHEDULED STOP POINT or TIMING POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN with its order in that JOURNEY PATTERN.
exclusion

Name: JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes:
An ordered list of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs and TIMING POINTs on a single ROUTE, describing the pattern of working for public transport vehicles.
NOTE1: A JOURNEY PATTERN may pass through the same POINT more than once.
NOTE2: The first point of a JOURNEY PATTERN is the origin; the last point is the destination.

Name: DEAD RUN PATTERN
Notes: A JOURNEY PATTERN to be used for DEAD RUNs.

Name: TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: A POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN which is a TIMING POINT.

Name: TIMING LINK IN JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes:
The position of a TIMING LINK in a JOURNEY PATTERN.
NOTE: This entity is needed if a TIMING LINK is repeated in the same JOURNEY PATTERN, and separate information is to be stored about each iteration of the TIMING LINK.

Name: TIMING POINT
Notes: A POINT against which the timing information necessary to build schedules may be recorded.

Name: GROUP OF TIMING LINKS
Notes:
A set of TIMING LINKs grouped together according to the similarity of TIME BANDs which are relevant to them.
NOTE: There may be a GROUP OF TIMING LINKS which covers all TIMING LINKs, for use when different GROUPs OF TIMING LINKS are not needed.

Name: TIMING LINK
Notes: An ordered pair of TIMING POINTs for which run times may be recorded.

Name: TIMING PATTERN
Notes: The subset of a JOURNEY PATTERN made up only of TIMING POINTs IN JOURNEY PATTERN.

Name: DEFAULT CONNECTION
Notes:
The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip. 
NOTE1: It specifies default times to be used to change from one mode of transport to another at an area or national level as specified by a TOPOGRAPHIC PLACE, STOP AREA or SITE ELEMENT. 
NOTE2: It may be further restricted to a specific MODE or OPERATOR or only apply in a particular direction of transfer, e.g., bus to rail may have a different time for rail to bus.

Name: DEFAULT CONNECTION END
Notes: One end of a DEFAULT CONNECTION.

Name: SITE CONNECTION END
Notes: One end of a SITE CONNECTION.

Name: SITE CONNECTION
Notes:
The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip, determined by physical locations, such as SITEs and/or its components and/or ENTRANCEs, in particular STOP PLACEs and/or its components.
NOTE: Different times may be necessary to cover the resulting distance, depending on the kind of passenger.

Name: CONNECTION END
Notes: One end of a CONNECTION.

Name: SERVICE LINK
Notes: A LINK between an ordered pair of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs.

Name: SERVICE PATTERN
Notes: The subset of a JOURNEY PATTERN made up only of STOP POINTs IN JOURNEY PATTERN.

Name: SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: The JOURNEY PATTERN for a (passenger carrying) SERVICE JOURNEY.

Name: SCHEDULED STOP POINT
Notes: A POINT where passengers can board or alight from vehicles.

Name: CONNECTION
Notes:
The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip, determined by a pair of points which may be either SCHEDULED STOP POINTs or VEHICLE MEETING POINTs.
NOTE: Different times may be necessary to cover the link between these points, depending on the kind of passenger.

Name: STOP AREA
Notes: A group of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs close to each other.

Name: TYPE OF STOP POINT
Notes: A classification of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs, used for instance to characterise the equipment to be installed at stops (post, shelter, seats, etc.).

Name: STOP POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: A POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN which is a SCHEDULED STOP POINT.
Renamed from TRAIN STOP ASSIGNMENT to PASSENGER BOARDING POSITION ASSIGNMENT.

Name: COMMON SECTION
Notes:
A part of a public transport network where the ROUTEs of several JOURNEY PATTERNs are going in parallel and where the synchronisation of SERVICE JOURNEYs may be planned and controlled with respect to commonly used LINKs and SCHEDULED STOP POINTs.
NOTE: COMMON SECTIONs are defined arbitrarily and need not cover the total lengths of topologically bundled sections.

Name: ROUTING CONSTRAINT ZONE
Notes:
A ZONE specifying constraints on activity when a journey is routed through it.
NOTE: Examples of routing constraints are "If you board in this ZONE, you can't alight in the same ZONE"; "If you board in this ZONE, you can alight only if the journey has passed through at least one STOP outside of the ZONE"; "Journey will go on only if there are passenger on board", etc.

Name: TRANSFER RESTRICTION
Notes: A constraint that can be applied on a CONNECTION or INTERCHANGE between two SCHEDULED STOP POINT, preventing or forbidding the passenger to use it.

Name: SERVICE EXCLUSION
Notes:
A constraint on the use of a service; the service, on this specific JOURNEY PATTERN (usually a FTS JOURNEY PATTERN) cannot operate when another (regular) service operates.
NOTE: This may occur only on subpart of the JOURNEY PATTERN, or only on one or some specific SCHEDULED STOP POINTS within the pattern.

Name: TYPE OF TRANSFER RESTRICTION
Notes: Classification of TRANSFER RESTRICTION, for example, allowed, allowed at certain times, etc.

Name: ALLOWED ZONE USE
Notes: Classification of allowed behaviour in zone, for example; cannot board in zone, must board in zone, cannot board and alight in same zone, etc.

Name: TIME DEMAND TYPE
Notes:
An indicator of traffic conditions or other factors which may affect vehicle run or wait times.
NOTE: It may be entered directly by the scheduler or defined by the use of TIME BANDs.

Name: TIME DEMAND TYPE ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The assignment of a TIME DEMAND TYPE to a TIME BAND depending on the DAY TYPE and GROUP OF TIMING LINKS.

Name: STOP ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT to a specific STOP PLACE, and also possibly a QUAY.

Name: PASSENGER STOP ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The default allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT to a specific STOP PLACE, and also possibly a QUAY.

Name: PASSENGER BOARDING POSITION ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The association of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT with a specific STOP PLACE and also possibly a QUAY and BOARDING POSITION; may be general for all types of vehicle at that stop, or specific to a VEHICLE TYPE such as a TRAIN, in which case a TRAIN COMPONENT may also be specified to indicate a specific carriage.

In the basic case, e.g., for buses and simple VEHICLE TYPES a STOP ASSIGNMENT for an individual BOARDING POSITION may apply regardless of VEHICLE TYPE.

In VEHICLE TYPES such as trains, a STOP ASSIGNMENT for an individual BOARDING POSITION may be specific to the VEHICLE TYPE (i.e. TRAIN type) and TRAIN COMPONENT, so that boarding positions may be related to individual carriages. 

NOTE: A VEHICLE JOURNEY STOP ASSIGNMENT (See Part 3) can be used to make an assignment for a specific VEHICLE JOURNEY or DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY. A DECK ENTRANCE ASSIGNMENT can further relate the doors of specific carriages of the train to specific boarding position.

Name: NAVIGATION PATH ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The allocation of a NAVIGATION PATH to a specific STOP POINT ASSIGNMENT, for example to indicate the path to be taken to make a CONNECTION.

Name: PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT
Notes: A public transport information piece of equipment, as for instance terminals (on street, at information desks, telematic, etc.) or printed material (leaflets displayed at stops, booklets, etc.).

Name: LOGICAL DISPLAY
Notes:
A set of data that can be assembled for assignment to a physical PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT or to a logical channel such as web or media; it is independent of any physical embodiment. 
NOTE: A LOGICAL DISPLAY may have a set of DISPLAY ASSIGNMENTS each of which associates a JOURNEY PATTERN whose journeys are to be shown at the LOGICAL DISPLAY, usually in the context of a specific SCHEDULED STOP POINT.

Name: TYPE OF PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT
Notes: A classification for PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT (e.g., next stop indicator, stop announcements, passenger information facility).

Name: DISPLAY ASSIGNMENT
Notes: The assignment of one SCHEDULED STOP POINT and one JOURNEY PATTERN to a PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT specifying that information on the SCHEDULED STOP POINT and the JOURNEY PATTERN will be provided (e.g., displayed, printed).

Name: INFRASTRUCTURE FRAME
Notes: A set of infrastructure network data (and other data logically related to these) to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.

Name: SERVICE FRAME
Notes: A set of network service data (and other data logically related to these) to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs has been assigned.

Name: SITE FRAME
Notes: A set of SITE data to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.

Name: EXTRA DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY
Notes: A DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY added to the PRODUCTION PLAN in addition to the long term planned NORMAL DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs.

Notes: A VEHICLE SERVICE taking place on a particular OPERATING DAY.

Name: DATED VEHICLE SERVICE PART
Notes: A VEHICLE SERVICE PART taking place on a particular OPERATING DAY.

Name: CALL
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the individual visit to a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a VEHICLE JOURNEY or DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: ARRIVAL
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the arrival to a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a VEHICLE JOURNEY or DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: CALL PART
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the arrival to or the departure from a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a VEHICLE JOURNEY or DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.
Note that the list of classes that can be attached to the <<TRANSMODEL VIEW>> classes is not conclusive.

Name: DEPARTURE
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the departure from a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a VEHICLE JOURNEY or DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.
Note that the list of classes that can be attached to the <<TRANSMODEL VIEW>> classes is not conclusive.

Name: DATED CALL
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the individual visit to a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: DATED ARRIVAL
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the arrival to a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: DATED CALL PART
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the arrival to or the departure from a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: DATED DEPARTURE
Notes: A view that brings together data relating to the departure from a POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.
Note that the list of classes that can be attached to the <<TRANSMODEL VIEW>> classes is not conclusive.

Name: PRODUCTION PLAN
Notes:
A reference version of production activities (service journeys, dead runs, duties, etc.).
NOTE: CONTROL ACTIONs are described with reference to the PRODUCTION PLAN they amend.

Name: LOGICAL VEHICLE
Notes: A theoretically available vehicle resource for an OPERATING DAY, foreseen to be monitored.

Name: VEHICLE DETECTING LOG ENTRY
Notes: A record of detected raw real-time data that is recognized to be related with a certain VEHICLE.

Name: VEHICLE DETECTING
Notes: An activity consisting in the identification of a vehicle at a certain time by a detection device and of collecting raw data, such as an absolute location of the vehicle.

Notes: An actual data detected in a VEHICLE DETECTING event, e.g., detection of an actual vehicle coupling, detection of an INCIDENT or detection of an actual relief.

Name: VEHICLE MONITORING LOG ENTRY
Notes: A record of computed information describing some aspect of how a certain LOGICAL VEHICLE performs in relation to the latest operation plan based on comparing information from detection devices with operational data.

Notes: A special service that is monitored as being operated by a LOGICAL VEHICLE.

The difference between the impeded and non-impeded passage of a LINK.
NOTE: It consists of slow down time, waiting time, and accelerating time.

Notes: The aspect (type of situation) addressed by the monitoring activity.
E.g., calculating an estimated passing time, noting an observed passing time

Name: MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY
Notes:
A journey that is monitored as being operated by a LOGICAL VEHICLE.
NOTE: According to the monitoring system capabilities, a MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY may be related to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY, or only to a JOURNEY PATTERN.

Name: VEHICLE MONITORING
Notes: An activity consisting in the assignment, at a certain time, of operational data to a monitored LOGICAL VEHICLE (e.g., that the vehicle is operating a certain MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY or has passed at a certain OBSERVED PASSING TIME at a POINT).

Name: MONITORED OPERATION
Notes: Operational data monitored in a VEHICLE MONITORING event (e.g., monitoring a LOGICAL VEHICLE, coupling to others, as operating a planned TRAIN BLOCK).

Name: OBSERVED PASSING TIME
Notes: The actual passing of a public transport vehicle at a pre-defined POINT during a MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: ESTIMATED PASSING TIME
Notes:
A time data, calculated from the latest available input, about when a public transport vehicle will pass a particular POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN on a specified DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.
NOTE: Mainly used to inform passengers about expected times of arrival and/or departure, but may also be used for monitoring and re-planning.

OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL
CONTROL ACTION
Notes: An action resulting from a decision taken by the controller causing an amendment of the operation planned in the PRODUCTION PLAN.
Note that in addition to the control actions shown here there are also Driver Control Actions defined in part 7 that inherit from CONTROL ACTION.

Name: GROUP OF CONTROL ACTIONS
Notes: A grouping of related CONTROL ACTIONs, usually either triggered by one "master" CONTROL ACTION (for example the closing of a stop point) or by a SITUATION (weather condition, road traffic, etc.).

Name: LOGICAL VEHICLE CANCELLATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in removing a LOGICAL VEHICLE from the production plan.

Name: VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT
Notes:
The assignment, or the cancellation of an assignment, of a physical VEHICLE to a LOGICAL VEHICLE.
NOTE: This assignment may be overridden by a further assignment.

Name: CHANGE OF VEHICLE
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in removing, at a certain point in time and space, all work assigned to a LOGICAL VEHICLE and of assigning it to another LOGICAL VEHICLE.

Name: VEHICLE CONTROL ACTION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION affecting the LOGICAL VEHICLE.

Name: VEHICLE WORK ASSIGNMENT
Notes:
The assignment, or the cancellation of an assignment, of a physical VEHICLE to a LOGICAL VEHICLE to some planned work, represented as DATED BLOCKs or as DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs.
NOTE: This assignment may be overridden by a further assignment.
exclusion

Name: LOGICAL VEHICLE CREATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in creating a completely new LOGICAL VEHICLE and assigning DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs to the new LOGICAL VEHICLE.

Name: CHANGE OF JOURNEY PATTERN
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in assigning a new JOURNEY PATTERN (and the ROUTE supporting it) to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: CHANGE OF JOURNEY TIMING
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in changing one or several characteristics of a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY, in particular the departure time of the journey.

Name: PARTIAL JOURNEY CANCELLATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in assigning a JOURNEY PATTERN that is a subset of the original JOURNEY PATTERN to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY; thus specifically expressing that a part of a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY has been cancelled.

Name: JOURNEY CANCELLATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in deleting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY from the latest valid plan.

Name: JOURNEY CREATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in adding a completely new DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY to the latest valid plan.

Name: ELEMENTARY JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION
Notes: A non-composite CONTROL ACTION affecting DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs.

Name: FLEXIBLE JOURNEY ACTIVATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in activating a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY that has a booking pre-condition.

Name: DEPARTURE LAG
Notes:
A CONTROL ACTION consisting of gradually shifting a set of departures at one POINT.
NOTE: It allows a change of the timetable without abrupt variations in the intervals.

Name: RESPACING
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION to respace departure times at one POINT after a journey or a vehicle has been added or cancelled, in order to preserve the regularity of intervals.

Name: COMPOSITE JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION affecting a set of DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs with a correlated set of adjustments.

Name: DEPARTURE EXCHANGE
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in permuting at one POINT the departure times of two or several DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs.

Name: RESORPTION
Notes:
A CONTROL ACTION consisting of progressively resorbing a delay on one DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY by rescheduling the departure times at one POINT of the following journeys.
NOTE: It is a way of maintaining regular intervals after a disturbance on a particular journey.

Name: INTERCHANGE CANCELLATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in deleting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE from the latest valid plan so that a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY no longer needs to wait for a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

Name: INTERCHANGE MODIFICATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION expressing that the duration a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY needs to wait for a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE is changed or that a different DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY is to wait for the feeder.

Name: INTERCHANGE CREATION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in adding a completely new DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE between a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY and a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY to the latest valid plan.

Name: INTERCHANGE CONTROL ACTION
Notes: A CONTROL ACTION affecting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE.

Name: CHANGE OF STOP POINT STATUS
Notes:
Change of the status of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT, a STOP PLACE or a QUAY, impacting all the DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs in a certain period of time.
NOTE: This CONTROL ACTION is mainly used for stop closing or opening, and will give rise to further actions such as CHANGE OF JOURNEY PATTERNs or PARTIAL JOURNEY CANCELLATIONs.

Name: OPERATIONAL EVENT
Notes:
Any event affecting the public transport operation (production follow-up, management of information or the technical functioning), occurring at a certain time and that is recorded in the system.
NOTE: An OPERATIONAL EVENT is generally causing a CONTROL ACTION.

Name: ALARM
Notes: An EVENT alerting the staff in charge of operations control on a probable dysfunction: operational threshold exceeded (e.g., delay), emergency call, failure, etc.

Name: VEHICLE INCIDENT
Notes: An INCIDENT concerning LOGICAL VEHICLEs.

Name: FACILITY OPERATIONAL EVENT
Notes: An OPERATIONAL EVENT concerning a FACILITY.

Name: SITE OPERATIONAL EVENT
Notes: An OPERATIONAL EVENT applying to a SITE.

Name: DRIVER INCIDENT
Notes: An INCIDENT concerning LOGICAL DRIVERs.

Name: INCIDENT
Notes: An unforeseen EVENT influencing the operation of the network.

Name: OPERATIONAL MESSAGE
Notes: An information exchange between an EMPLOYEE (e.g., a controller), a LOGICAL DRIVER or a LOGICAL VEHICLE, used to inform about a CONTROL ACTION or an EVENT.

Name: CALL FOR REPAIRS
Notes: A MESSAGE of a controller sent to a GARAGE to ask for repair of a VEHICLE.

Name: CALL FOR MEANS
Notes: A MESSAGE of a controller sent to a PARKING POINT to ask for the activation of resources in stand-by.

Notes: A sequence or set of FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENTs, grouped together to be validated in one go.

Name: CONTROLLABLE ELEMENT
Notes: The smallest controllable element of public transport consumption, all along which any VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT remains valid.

Notes: Describes different types of Fare product.

Notes: A FARE PRODUCT that is marketed together with a Public Transport FARE PRODUCT.

SALES DISCOUNT RIGHT = A FARE PRODUCT allowing a customer to benefit from discounts when purchasing SALES OFFER PACKAGEs. For example a rail card. Distinct from an ENTITLEMENT PRODUCT - which also gives a discount but is not itself a FARE PRODUCT (For example a Veteran's card). Quite often a SALE DISCOUNT RIGHT is bundled into a SALES OFFER PACKAGE with another FARE PRODUCT, for example a season ticket to travel on a train route might give the right to buy other train tickets at a discount.

Name: USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT
Notes: A FARE PRODUCT allowing a customer to benefit from discounts when consuming VALIDABLE ELEMENTs.

PREASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT: A FARE PRODUCT consisting of one or several VALIDABLE ELEMENTs, specific to a CHARGING METHOD. Used for trips bought in advance or postpaid.

AMOUNT OF PRICE UNIT = A FARE PRODUCT consisting in a stored value of PRICE UNITs: an amount of money on an electronic purse, amount of units on a value card etc. For example, a coupon with 10 points on it, a subway token, a smart card holding 8 Euros in stored value.

Name: AMOUNT OF PRICE UNIT
Notes: A FARE PRODUCT consisting in a stored value of PRICE UNITs: an amount of money on an electronic purse, amount of units on a value card etc.

Name: ACCESS RIGHT IN PRODUCT
Notes: A VALIDABLE ELEMENT as a part of a PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT, including its possible order in the set of all VALIDABLE ELEMENTs grouped together to define the access right assigned to that PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT.

ENTITLEMENT PRODUCT: A precondition to access a service or to purchase a FARE PRODUCT, issued by an organisation that may not necessarily be a PT operator (e.g., military card). The ENTITLEMENT REQUIRED validity parameter of a SALES OFFER PACKAGE or a FARE PRODUCT can specify which ENTITLEMENT PRODUCT (s) are required in order to buy a give FARE PRODUCT

CAPPED DISCOUNT RIGHT: A specialisation of SALE DISCOUNT RIGHT where the discount is expressed as a rule specifying a ceiling within a given time interval. For example, the London Oyster card fare, which charges for each journey until travel equivalent to a day pass has been consumed, after which further travel is free on that day. Fare can be capped to an amount or linked to the price of another product within a given USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD.

THIRD PARTY PRODUCT: A FARE PRODUCT that is marketed together with a Public Transport FARE PRODUCTs. Sometimes a SALES OFFER PACKAGE includes items from another operator for which no fare description is available, but nonetheless needs to be understood as part of the offering. These can be represented as THIRD PARTY PRODUCTS.

Name: PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT
Notes: A FARE PRODUCT consisting of one or several VALIDABLE ELEMENTs, specific to a CHARGING <font color="#0f0f0f">MOMENT</font>.

USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT: A FARE PRODUCT allowing a customer to benefit from discounts when consuming VALIDABLE ELEMENTs. Distinct from a SALES DISCOUNT RIGHT which is the right to purchase additional products at a discount, the USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT gives a cheaper rate when consuming access rights already included in a product. Quite often a USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT is bundled into a SALES OFFER PACKAGE with another FARE PRODUCT.

Name: TYPE OF FREQUENCY OF USE
Notes: A classification of FREQUENCY OF USE.

Notes: A CUSTOMER RESERVATION ENTRY recording the availability of spots for given TRIP at a given moment in time.

Name: CUSTOMER RESERVATION CREATION EVENT
Notes: The creation or modification of a reservation by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER, possibly without purchase.

Name: CUSTOMER RESERVATION CANCELLATION EVENT
Notes: The cancellation of a reservation by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER.

Name: CUSTOMER RESERVATION EVENT
Notes: An event relating to reservations

Name: CUSTOMER SPOT AVAILABILITY EVENT
Notes: An action to check the availability of a SPOT for reservation to a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER for a given trip.

Name: SPOT ALLOCATION METHOD
Notes: Method for allocating seating, and other bookable spots (for example; open seating, system assigned, self assigned from available, etc.).

Name: SPOT AVAILABILITY STATUS
Notes: Current status of allocation of PASSENGER SEAT, e.g., Available, Reserved, Booked, Blocked, etc.

Name: PASSENGER SPOT ALLOCATION
Notes: Current ALLOCATION of a LOCATABLE SPOT such as a passenger seat or on-board vehicle space to a customer <font color="#445469">between two STOP POINTs. </font>

Name: VEHICLE JOURNEY SPOT ALLOCATION
Notes: The set of current allocations of on-board LOCATABLE SPOTs (i.e., seats, vehicle berths, etc.) for a given NORMAL DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY.
PASSENGER SPOT ALLOCATION assigns a LOCATABLE SPOT (e.g. seat) to a specific passenger between two SCHEDULED STOP POINTS the JOURNEY PATTERN of a specific NORMAL DATED JOURNEY
E.g., available, in use, reserved, out of service

PASSENGER SPOT ALLOCATION records the allocation of a specific seat (PASSENGER SPOT) between two stops (SCHEDULED STOP POINTs) on a specific journey and date (NORMAL DATED JOURNEY) to a specific passenger (TRANSPORT CUSTOMER).

VEHICLE JOURNEY SPOT ALLOCATION contains all the allocations for the journey

EQUIPMENT associated with a spot can specify detailed quantitative properties of a seat or bed in a spot, e.g., seat height, adjustable, power sockets, etc.
NB FACILITies can be used for simple list of named amenities.
The potentially bookable seats (i.e. LOCATABLE SPOTs) available on a given journey are specified by the DECK PLAN associated with the JOURNEY or JOURNEY PART.

PASSENGER SPOT ALLOCATION records the allocation of a specific seat (PASSENGER SPOT) between two stops (SCHEDULED STOP POINTs) on a specific journey and date (NORMAL DATED JOURNEY) to a specific passenger (TRANSPORT CUSTOMER).

VEHICLE JOURNEY SPOT ALLOCATION contains all the allocations for the journey
E.g., available, in use, reserved, out of service

Name: TRAVEL PREFERENCES
Notes: Explicit or implicit preferences for travel of the actual TRANSPORT CUSTOMER to be used when making requests.

Name: CONVENTIONAL MODE TRAVEL PREFERENCES
Notes: Preferences for trip optimisation, e.g., least changes, fastest, least walking, etc.

Name: FAVOURITE PLACE
Notes: A designated favourite place for the user that will be used repeatedly on requests, such as Home, Work, Gym, etc

Name: ALTERNATIVE MODE TRAVEL PREFERENCES
Notes: Preferences of the TRANSPORT CUSTOMER that may be used when making requests for trips that include ALTERNATIVE MODE LEGs.

Name: CYCLING TRAVEL PREFERENCES
Notes: Preferences the TRANSPORT CUSTOMER may use when making trip requests that include cycling legs.

Name: HIKING TRAVEL PREFERENCES
Notes: Preferences the TRANSPORT CUSTOMER to be used when making requests that include hiking legs.

Attributes shown for preferences and specialisations of TRAVEL PREFERENCES for different mode are just indicative. Further specialisations and attributes might be relevant for an actual implementation. For example, DRIVING TRAVEL PREFERENCES with satnav, automatic transmission, etc.

Name: PREFERRED MODE
Notes: A preference by the user to travel by a specific mode and/or submode.

Name: OFFERED TRAVEL SPECIFICATION
Notes: A set of parameters giving details of the offered consumption of access rights associated with a SALES PACKAGE OFFER or a CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE, (e.g., origin and destination of a travel, class of travel, etc.).

Name: TRAVEL SPECIFICATION
Notes: A set of parameters giving details of an intended consumption of access rights by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER (e.g., origin and destination of a travel, class of travel, etc.).

Name: SPECIFIC PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
Notes: A VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT specifying practical parameters during a TRAVEL SPECIFICATION, within a given fare structure (e.g., the origin or destination zone in a zone-counting system).

Name: REQUESTED TRAVEL SPECIFICATION
Notes: A set of parameters giving details of an intended consumption of access rights requested by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER (e.g., origin and destination of a travel, class of travel, etc.).

Name: LEG IN TRAVEL SPECIFICATION
Notes: RIDE LEG offered by TRAVEL SPECIFICATION, in Sequence

Name: CUSTOMER PURCHASE STATUS
Notes: A classification of possible statuses of CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE, e.g., booked, paid for, consumed.

Name: CUSTOMER PURCHASE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
Notes: A VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT specifying detailed parameters corresponding to a particular CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE, chosen from those available for a given fare structure (e.g. the origin or destination zone in a zone-counting system).

Name: CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE
Notes: A purchase of a SALES OFFER PACKAGE by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER, giving access rights corresponding to those of one or several FARE PRODUCTs materialised as one or several TRAVEL DOCUMENTs.

Name: CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE PRICE
Notes: A specialisation of FARE PRICE that defines the price of a CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE.

Name: CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE ELEMENT
Notes: A purchase of a SALES OFFER PACKAGE ELEMENT by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER, with an indication of all selected parameters.

RESPONSIBILITY SETs may be associated with any ENTITY (i.e., SALES OFFER PACKAGE, FARE PRODUCT, CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE, TRAVEL DOCUMENT, etc). to indicate the ROLEs to be played by different ORGANISATIONs.
RESPONSIBILITY SET can be used to assign to TRAVEL DOCUMENT and CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE ELEMENT various FARE MANAGEMENT and TECHNOLOGY ORGANISATION ROLES.

Name: FR Fare Management Role MODEL
Notes: The Fare Management Role model describes the corporate actors who provide transport services.

Name: FARE SECURITY MANAGER ROLE
Notes: <font color="#0f0f0f">The ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION ROLE of establishing and coordinating a security policy for fare data across the provider organisations, and of the certifying and auditing of organisations, applications, etc., for their conformance to the security policy.</font>

Name: FARE DATA COLLECTOR ROLE
Notes:
The role of collecting and forwarding fare data between the various parties concerned with product delivery, such as PRODUCT RETAILER, PRODUCT OWNER, etc.
NOTE: May be undertaken by a separate intermediary.

Name: FARE PRODUCT RETAILER ROLE
Notes:
The role of an organisation to sell products to TRANSPORT CUSTOMERs, as authorised by the holder of a FARE PRODUCT OWNER ROLE.
NOTE: The FARE PRODUCT RETAILER ROLE may be undertaken by the same party as the FARE PRODUCT OWNER ROLE, the ACCOUNT PROVIDER ROLE, or a secondary outlet such as a TRAVEL AGENT, newsagent, or other third party, etc.

Name: FARE REGISTRAR ROLE
Notes: The ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION ROLE of coordinating the issue of unique registration codes (for example, by determining rules for generating unique codes) for data linked to fare management such as FARE CONTRACTs, TRAVEL DOCUMENTs, etc.

Name: FARE ORGANISATION ROLE
Notes: Any corporate role in providing or managing transport services.

Name: FARE PRODUCT ISSUER ROLE
Notes:
A role of an organisation introduced when there are a large number of fare product owners and a large number of distributors.
NOTE: The FARE PRODUCT ISSUER ROLE makes a portfolio of products available to a product distributor to be sold via product retailers to TRANSPORT CUSTOMERs.

Name: FARE PRODUCT ATTRIBUTOR ROLE
Notes: The role of being an agent of a FARE PRODUCT OWNER, i.e., the role of an intermediary organisation to whom certain responsibilities have been delegated by the FARE PRODUCT OWNER, for instance to provide the technical implementation of the products defined by the FARE PRODUCT OWNER.

Name: FARE PRODUCT DISTRIBUTOR ROLE
Notes: <font color="#0f0f0f">The role, in large networks, of organising and accounting for the wholesale distribution of FARE PRODUCTs, as delegated by the FARE PRODUCT OWNER ROLE and to supply products to the FARE PRODUCT RETAILER ROLE.</font>

Name: FARE PRODUCT OWNER ROLE
Notes: The role of the organisation which has commercial ownership of a FARE PRODUCT and is responsible for specifying pricing, usage conditions and commercial rules for the product, for ensuring there are processes for marketing and retailing the product, customer payment, control and validation, back office accounting and settlement and for customer service.

Name: FR Fare Management Role Associations MODEL
PAYMENT PROVIDER ROLE
Notes: The role of channelling funds from the CUSTOMER to the FARE PRODUCT RETAILER for travel services, and particularly for usage-based travel products (e.g., EMV provider, ApplePay, PayPal, Android Pay, etc.).

Name: IDENTITY PROVIDER ROLE
Notes:
The role of supplying a trusted identity token that can be associated with a CUSTOMER ACCOUNT, TRAVEL DOCUMENT, etc.
NOTE: The IDENTITY PROVIDER ROLE may be undertaken by transport AUTHORITies and OPERATORs, but also non-transport organisations, such as governments central and local, mobile network operators, or online service providers (e.g., Google, Facebook) and banks.

Name: MEDIUM APPLICATION OWNER ROLE
Notes: For media-centric products, the APPLICATION OWNER ROLE has commercial ownership of the software MEDIA APPLICATION hosting a product and is contracted by the PRODUCT OWNER for the use of the application with the customer.

Name: MEDIA PROVIDER ROLE
Notes:
The role of supplying the media used for the TRAVEL DOCUMENT, that is a physical support containing a machine readable/writable data/processor application.
NOTE: This can include transport industry smartcards, payment industry contactless cards, public sector issued cards, mobile phones or paper (for barcodes), new formats such as watches and key fobs, and NFC enabled devices.

Name: MEDIUM APPLICATION PROVIDER ROLE
Notes: For media-centric products, the APPLICATION PROVIDER supplies the software application that hosts a TRAVEL DOCUMENT and presents it to CONTROL DEVICEs for automatic control and validation.

Name: ACCOUNT PROVIDER ROLE
Notes: In Account Based Ticketing, the ACCOUNT PROVIDER provides the online account by means of which the product is delivered. Normally this involves a direct relationship with the CUSTOMER, though it may also be done as a white-labelled service for another party.

Name: FR Fare Transport Customer Role MODEL
Notes: The Fare User Role model describes the human actors who use transport services.

Name: FC Control Means MODEL
Notes: Description of the available means and devices with which validation and control of fares may be undertaken.

Name: FC Access Right Validation MODEL
Notes: Description of control and validation record created by customer interaction.

Name: GROUP MEMBER ROLE
Notes: The role of a passenger travelling under the access rights granted by a GROUP TICKET.

Name: PASSENGER ROLE
Notes: The general role of consuming a travel service.

Name: OFFENDER ROLE
Notes: The role enacted by someone attempting to travel with no or insufficient access rights.

Name: INDIVIDUAL PASSENGER ROLE
Notes: The role of a passenger consuming a travel service as a single individual.

Name: INDIVIDUAL PURCHASER ROLE
Notes: The role of a person in purchasing a FARE PRODUCT as a private individual; often, but not necessarily, the same as the PASSENGER ROLE.

Name: COMPANION ROLE
Notes: The role of accompanying another passenger under the access rights granted by the other passenger's ticket.

Name: CORPORATE PURCHASER ROLE
Notes: The role of purchasing FARE PRODUCTs on behalf of a corporate body such as a company, school, government department, etc.

Name: PURCHASER ROLE
Notes: The role of the party who pays for a travel service for one or more TRANSPORT CUSTOMERs.
1. Customer purchase of TRAVEL DOCUMENT indicating access rights - i.e., Product Fare Structure of VALIDABLE/ CONTROLLABLE elements that can be controlled.
2. Result of travel : control and marking (also called 'Cancellation' of validable elements) as CONTROLLED ACCESSes and VALIDATED ACCESSes.
3. Results of the Control & Validation Process: CONTROL ENTRies and VALIDATION ENTRies.

Name: OTHER CONTROL MEANS
Notes: A particular means other than a control device, for example a manual procedure, used to control apply control processes.

1. Device parameters (from a DEVICE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT) are compared with validity parameters (from VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENTs) to make a control.

2. The results are recorded on a CONTROL ENTRY (using CONTROL PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT(s)).

Name: CONTROL TYPE
Notes: A classification of passenger controls, e.g., entry, exit, en route or occasional controls.

Name: DEVICE RELATED CONTROL MEANS
Notes: A specific device constituting the CONTROL MEANS to control TRAVEL DOCUMENTs.

Name: CONTROL MEANS
Notes: A particular means (control device or manual control procedure) used to control TRAVEL DOCUMENTs.
Control means reads travel document and checks purchase against control context.

Name: CONTROL RECORD
Notes: A LOG ENTRY recording general audit properties of a validation or control action.

Name: CONTROL PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
Notes: An ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT relating a fare collection parameter to a CONTROL ENTRY.

Name: CONTROL ENTRY
Notes: The description of a control action, i.e., the comparison of actual and current parameters (time, location, etc.) to the access rights to which the holder of a TRAVEL DOCUMENT is entitled.

Validation compares parameters from device or other control means (DEVICE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT) with those of TRAVEL DOCUMENT and / or CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE (CUSTOMER PURCHASE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT) and creates VALIDATED ACCESS with VALIDATION PARAMETER ASSIGNMENTS to record validated parameters.

Name: VALIDATED ACCESS
Notes: A validated use of a VALIDABLE ELEMENT, composed of ACCESSED FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENTs.

Name: VALIDATION PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
Notes: An ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT relating a fare collection parameter to a VALIDATED ACCESS or one of its components.

Name: OFFENCE
Notes: A log entry providing data on a violation of fare rules.

Name: VALIDATION ENTRY
Notes: The result of the comparison between one or several CONTROL ENTRies and the theoretical access rights attached to the TRAVEL DOCUMENT controlled, validating the right to consume and possibly providing a DEBIT or one or more OFFENCEs.

Name: ACCESSED FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENT
Notes: A validated use of a FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENT, composed of CONTROLLED ACCESSes.

Name: TYPE OF OFFENCE
Notes: A classification of OFFENCE, for example wrong CLASS OF SEAT, not valid for PRODUCT CATEGORY, etc.

Name: DEVICE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
Notes: An ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT expressing the location (or other fixed parameters) of a CONTROL MEANS.

Name: CONTROLLED ACCESS
Notes: A validated use of a CONTROLLABLE ELEMENT.

Name: FE Passenger Travel Control Event MODEL
FE Passenger Travel Control Log Entry MODEL
Notes: Description of PASSENGER CONTROL ENTRies that result from customer travel.

Name: PASSENGER SECURITY LIST CHECK EVENT
Notes: A check of some aspect of the passengers travel credentials against a SECURITY LIST, usually triggered by another PASSENGER TRAVEL CONTROL EVENT such as check in at the start of a trip.

Name: CONTROL PASSENGER TRIP EVENT
Notes: The control of the consumption of access rights by the inspection of a TRAVEL DOCUMENT by a <font color="#0f0f0f">travel document inspector</font>.

Name: PASSENGER CHECK IN EVENT
Notes: A passenger action to check in at the start of a trip.

Name: PASSENGER WAY POINT EVENT
Notes: A passenger action to check in at a way point along a trip.

Name: PASSENGER TRAVEL CONTROL EVENT
Notes: An event concerned with validating or controlling a passengers use of the transport network.

Name: PASSENGER ACTIVATE TRIP EVENT
Notes: A passenger action to initiate the consumption of access rights, usually at the start of a trip, for example by stamping a ticket at a validator device, or by an online interaction.

Name: PASSENGER CHECK OUT EVENT
Notes: A passenger action to check out at the end of a trip.

Name: CONTROL REVERT FARE EVENT
Notes:
A control action to reverse the consumption of access rights, usually at the start of a trip, for example by restoring the validity of a ticket that has been accidentally marked as used.
NOTE: Usually done by a ticket controller.

Access rights from CUSTOMER PURCHASE PACKAGE or TRAVEL DOCUMENT are compared with context of inspection (e.g., at entrance/exit, or onboard as DEVICE PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT) to create validated ACCESSED FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENTs with validated parameters (VALIDATION PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT).

Name: PASSENGER WAY POINT ENTRY
Notes: A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording a passenger checking in at a way point while in a trip so as to indicate travel by a specific itinerary.

Name: FARE TRIP ACTIVATION ENTRY
Notes: <font color="#0f0f0f">A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the initiation of the consumption of access rights by a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER making a trip, for example by means of marking a TRAVEL DOCUMENT using a ticket validator machine.</font>

Name: PASSENGER CHECK OUT ENTRY
Notes:
A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the check-out of a passenger at a barrier or validation point at the end of a journey.
NOTE: May trigger post payment.

Name: CONTROL PASSENGER TRIP ENTRY
Notes:
A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the control of the consumption of access rights by the inspection of a TRAVEL DOCUMENT by a TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONTROLLER.
NOTE: May include marking (cancellation) of the TRAVEL DOCUMENT.

Name: PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY
Notes: An abstract VALIDATION ENTRY relating to control of the PASSENGER.

Name: PASSENGER CHECK IN ENTRY
Notes:
A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the check-out of a passenger at a barrier or validation point at the end of a journey.
NOTE: May trigger prepayment.

Name: CONTROL FARE REVERSION ENTRY
Notes:
<font color="#0f0f0f">A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the reversal of the consumption of access rights, </font>usually at the start of a trip, for example by restoring the validity of a ticket that has been accidentally marked as used.
NOTE: Usually done by a ticket controller.

Name: FE Revenue Protection Log Entry MODEL
Notes: Description of revenue protection entries that take place through customer interaction with a fare management system.

Name: FE Travel Match Log Entry MODEL
NO CHECK IN DETECTED ENTRY
Notes:
A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the detection that a passenger has failed to check in at the end of a journey.
NOTE: This may be triggered by a subsequent check in or by back office processes looking for unmatched way point check in and check out events within a specified window.

Name: PASSENGER USED SAME STOP ENTRY
Notes: A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the detection of a passenger re-entering a station within a threshold period.

Name: NO CHECK OUT DETECTED ENTRY
Notes:
A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the detection that a passenger has failed to check out at the end of a journey.
NOTE: This may be triggered by a subsequent check in or by back office processes looking for unmatched check in and check out events within a specified window.

Name: UNMATCHED TRAVEL ENTRY
Notes: A PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY recording the detection that an incompletely recorded trip has been detected.

Name: ACCOUNT PROCESSING EVENT
Notes: An event initiated by the processing of a CUSTOMER ACCOUNT by an Account Based Ticketing system.

Name: ACCOUNT DETECT SUSPICIOUS BEHAVIOUR EVENT
Notes: The detection by an Account Based Ticketing system of suspicious or fraudulent use of a TRAVEL DOCUMENT, for example being used in two different places at the same time.

Name: ACCOUNT DETECT REENTRY EVENT
Notes: The detection by an Account Based Ticketing system of reentry at the same station within a specified threshold period.

Name: ACCOUNT DETECT NO CHECK OUT EVENT
Notes:
The detection that a passenger has failed to check out at the end of a trip.
NOTE: This may be triggered by a subsequent check in on a new journey or by back office processes looking for unmatched check in and check out events within a specified window.

Name: ACCOUNT DETECT TRIP EVENT
Notes: The detection by an Account Based Ticketing system of a trip made by the user that needs to be accounted for.

Name: ACCOUNT DETECT NO CHECK IN EVENT
Notes:
The detection that a passenger has failed to check in at the beginning of a trip.
NOTE: This may be triggered by a subsequent check out or by back office processes looking for unmatched check in and check out events within a specified window.

Name: SECURITY LIST CHECK FAIL ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY recording the failure to pass a security check, either through being on a BLACKLIST or not being on a required WHITE LIST.

Name: NO ACCESS RIGHTS ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY recording the detection of a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER travelling without having purchased access rights

Name: NO PROOF ON PERSON ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY recording the detection of a customer who claims to have purchased access rights but has no proof, e.g., TRAVEL DOCUMENT on their person.

Name: TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONFISCATION ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY recording the confiscation of a TRAVEL DOCUMENT from a TRANSPORT CUSTOMER because of an OFFENCE.

Name: REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY
Notes: An abstract FARE CONTRACT ENTRY representing the recording of an event relating to revenue protection.

Name: SUSPICIOUS BEHAVIOUR ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION EVENT recording the detection of suspicious behaviour.

Name: INSUFFICIENT ACCESS RIGHTS ENTRY
Notes: A REVENUE PROTECTION ENTRY recording the result of the comparison between one or several CONTROL ENTRies and the theoretical access rights attached to the TRAVEL DOCUMENT controlled, detecting insufficient rights to consume and possibly giving rise to a FARE DEBIT or one or more OFFENCEs.
A SECURITY LIST ALLOW ENTRY records the clearing of a item from a BLACK LIST or its addition to a WHITE LIST.

SECURITY LIST FAIL ENTRY is created when a TRAVEL DOCUMENT, CUSTOMER, etc., is found to be on a BLACK LIST or not on a required WHITE LIST. Normally the check will be triggered by another travel event such as PASSENGER CHECK IN, PASSENGER CHECK OUT ENTRY etc and so be associated with a specific PASSENGER TRAVEL ENTRY.
A SECURITY LIST DENY ENTRY records the placing of a item on a BLACK LIST or removal from a WHITE LIST.

Name: FARE FRAME
Notes: A set of FARE data elements to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.

Name: FARE FRAME DEFAULTS
Notes: A set of pricing parameters and values to apply to an individual element in the FARE FRAME if no explicit value is specified on the element.
NB Lower level detail elements are omitted.
NB Lower level detail elements are omitted.

Name: SALES TRANSACTION FRAME
Notes: A set of SALES TRANSACTION data elements to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.

Name: FARE PRICE FRAME
Notes: A set of FARE PRICE data elements to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.
NB Lower level detail elements are omitted.

Name: CONTROL AND VALIDATION FRAME
Notes: A set of Validation and Control data elements to which the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs have been assigned.
